dct_description_sm: This project addresses the lack of documented diatom floristic studies from northern Qubec and Labrador. It provides a first detailed inventory of freshwater diatoms in this vast territory. Several lakes were sampled in order to analyse their recent diatom assemblages in the surface sediments and their environmental conditions (water chemistry and physical characteristics, catchment characteristics, etc.). A multivariate statistical approach was adopted in order to establish which environmental variables govern the observed distributional patterns. The autecological preferences of the diatom taxa were first estimated, and then the variance of diatom assemblages along two latitudinal gradients from boreal, subarctic to arctic conditions was analysed. The applicability and performance of weighted-averaging partial least squares (WA-PLS) inference models on the diatom data was then assessed, resulting in three new transfer functions for use in diatom-based paleolimnological studies in northern Qubec and Labrador. The statistical results presented here include some new taxonomic designations.
dct_title_s: Limnological data and diatom distributions in northern Qubec and Labrador lakes
